newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ATHLETICS-EZINWA SWEEPS INDOOR SPRINTS IN MOSCOW.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-EZINWA SWEEPS INDOOR SPRINTS IN MOSCOW.

text.p: Nigeria's Osmond Ezinwa swept the sprint honours at the Russian winter indoor meeting in Moscow on Tuesday, taking both the 60 and 200 metres with some ease.
Ezinwa won the 200 metres in 21.38 seconds, with Hungary's Miklos Gyulai, son of International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) chairman Istvan Gyulai, coming in second at 21.57.
The Nigerian clocked 6.70 to take the 60 metres, 0.06 seconds ahead of Pavel Galkin of Russia.

The absence of Jamaica's Juliet Cuthbert left Russian indoor specialist Irina Privalova with a simple task in the women's 60 metres. Privalova won in 7.08, close to the year's best 7.02 she ran in Lievin, France, on Sunday.
Russian team mate Natalya Voronova won the 200 metres in 23.15 seconds.

William Tanui won the men's 1,500 metres in 3 minutes 39.40 seconds, ahead of Britain's second-placed John Mayock and Irish veteran Marcus O'Sullivan. Fellow Kenyan Moses Kiptanui's absence appeared to take some of the pressure off Tanui.
Russia's athletics authorities, struggling for cash after financial troubles at the state-run National Sports Fund, cut the prize money for the event to $100,000 from $300,000 last year.

Money problems have also meant Russian athletes, who gather in the southern city of Volgograd this weekend for the national indoor meeting, have had little chance to train together over the winter for next month's world indoor championships in Paris.
